items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: Who was the band leader? I was the band leader. Mm-hmm. And who'd you have with you then? I had D.D. George Lewis, Clay Badge.

ctx.x: What was it before you went in? Oh, it was a restaurant and bar. Used to have seafood, you know, thing like that. And the bar and port. And, uh, where the dance division is now, that was open. That was open between there and the house in the back, which is the home. They lived there and they had empty light in between. They closed the lot and built a dance hall.

Yeah. Mm-hmm. That's the beginning of that. Oh, I see. So you were the first band in there then? No, no. Mealy. Mealy was the first band in there. And they didn't stay there too long, I don't think, before they got me in there, before I was down there. Oh. Well, who was the band leader when you went to Lutches? Who was the band leader? I was the band leader. Mm-hmm. And who'd you have with you then? I had D.D. George Lewis, Clay Badge. stuff with stuff That's when I got a job. I was working at the Kingfish.

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1960-01-25
items.q: And that's where Billy got, uh, boys fired and brought Dede in there.

ctx.x: Fantastic. Who was in the band then?

There was only four of us in there. It was Billy, when we first started it was Burtz. Burtz Stevenson was playing trumpet. It was Burtz, myself, Billy, and uh, a fella by the name of McGee, playing drum. Dede, he was working further down on Decatur Street, between St. Philip and uh, Dumaine, right close to where there's Vincent. The Lucas have the hardware. And then they, they fell in love with one another. And they got married. I was, I was the best man for their wedding. And that's where Billy got, uh, boys…
He came by and heard you there? Yes.

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-10-12
items.q: And he hired me, Billy, and a drummer called B.G.

ctx.x: So, okay, can you remember the time when you were playing with Ivan Thomas, when he was murdered? Yeah, sure. Can you tell us something about that? One thing I'd like to know is, can you remember any of the other people in the band? Yeah. Pomp. Pomp. Changer. Bruce Robinson, the piano. Walter Preston playing banjo. Chani on the drum. Steve Antonis. Uh-huh. And a young footballer named Al was playing tennis. Uh-huh. Those old boys were in that band at that time. He didn't have a bass player? No, he was using two…

School. I have a kid. Nick's symphony. His father had a grocery store. About stuff like stuff That's how I got to find it with Nick. He liked it so much, so... He liked to run a business, and he really runs a business really good. I'd better complain about Nick, but he still runs my business, right? He does not? He's alright. I mean, he's not in music. No, he's alive. He's alive. Yeah. Um, can you remember how long he was your manager, and when Dorothy Tate took over? Can you remember, I've never been able to…

items.q: Yes, George Lewis and his wife, Jeannette.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. We just lived together. Bill Rossman. Yeah, we're watching.

Yeah, actually, for all the nice boys and David Wyckoff, they were the ones who put up the money for the kids, I remember now. Let's see. Maybe I can get you to turn it off for a minute now, okay? Off. Time to start off. I don't know. Oh, no, I haven't been to Florida. Have you been to Florida? Where are you from? I'm from Florida. What part? Pensacola. Pensacola? Yeah. Can I embarrass you? What's your age? Now, what year were you born in? 1970. Born in 1970 over there? And what's your exact birthday? June the…

See? What are they calling you now? It's from the Boudoir. It has to be from the Boudoir. That's my handle. That's the handle you put on that.
